ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $\angle C=30^\circ$, and $AD \perp BC$ at $D$. $BE$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, and it intersects $AD$ at point $P$. If $AP=3$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because \angle A=90^\circ$, $\angle C=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC=60^\circ$, \\
$\because BE$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, \\
$\therefore \angle ABP=\angle DBP=30^\circ$, \\
$\because AD\perp BC$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAD=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle PAB=\angle PBA$, \\
$\therefore BP=AP=3$, \\
In $Rt\triangle PBD$, $PD=\frac{1}{2}PB=\frac{3}{2}$, \\
$\therefore AD=AP+PD=\frac{9}{2}$, \\
In $Rt\triangle ADC$, $AC=2AD=\boxed{9}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC; B, D, C are on the same horizontal straight line, and A is above. Line segment AD is perpendicular from A to BC, intersecting BC at D; point P is located on AD. Line segment BE starts from B, passes through P, and extends to point E on AC; therefore B, P, E are collinear, and BP is the part of angle bisector BE inside triangle ABD. Reasoning: It is known that ∠A=90°, ∠C=30°, so ∠ABC=180°-90°-30°=60°. Because D is on BC, ∠ABD=∠ABC=60°. Also because AD⊥BC, ∠ADB=90°, hence triangle ABD is a 30°-60°-90° triangle, and ∠BAD=30°. In this triangle, AB is the hypotenuse, and BD is the short right-angle side opposite 30°, so AB:BD=2:1. Since BE is the angle bisector of ∠ABC, and BP is collinear with BE, D is on BC, BP bisects ∠ABD. By the angle bisector theorem in triangle ABD, AP/PD=AB/BD=2/1. It is known that AP=3, therefore PD=3/2. Thus AD=AP+PD=3+3/2=9/2. In right triangle ADC, ∠ADC=90°, ∠C=30°, AD is the side opposite 30°, and AC is the hypotenuse, so AC=2AD=2×9/2=9.
